newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end up on post-poll optimism.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end up on post-poll optimism.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended up but off highs on Friday in a continuing wave of optimism following this week's general elections, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index closed 0.95 percent higher at 696.03 points after hitting a high of 699.72 points earlier. Gainers led losers by 68 to 43, with 68 counters unchanged.
Total volume was estimated at about 861 billion rupiah, compared with 784.3 billion rupiah on election day on Thursday.
There was a brief bout of nerves at midsession on news of clashes in the island of Madura but sentiment soon recovered, brokers said.
But one analsyt with a Hong Kong-based firm said the brief drop in the index was also caused by profit-taking as some counters had made sharp gains on the week.

"If you notice since last Monday, the index rose sharply. Some investors must think it's better to take profit as they believed the market has not returned to its normal condition yet," the analyst said.
Another analyst with a Singapore-based firm expected that the market would be mixed in the coming week as investors remain concerned over possibilities of post-election violence.
The analyst, however, said that there was further upside potential in the coming week as Thursday's general election was concluded relatively peacefully.
"After the smooth general election, many foreigners will come back to the Indonesian market, at least for the short-term. If there is an opportunity to make short-term gains, why not," he said.
First tier counters such as Telkom, Indofood and Bank Negara Indonesia were among the targets of buyers after they announced good first quarter results, brokers said.
Local-led buying was seen on counters belonging to the Lippo Group, which was also boosted by higher-than-expected first quarter results of its units, brokers said.
Buying interest on Hero Supermarket was also strong on renewed speculation that rival retailer Multipolar would buy a stake in it in the second half of this year, brokers said.
Property firm Surya Semesta was the most active stock with about 46.7 million shares traded. Brokers said the rise was due to expectations of higher-than-expected net profit in the first quarter.
